item.text:
**Assessment**
Mixed, leaning positive on welfare delivery. In 2024 Jokowi had real pro-welfare actions and outcomes, especially in health, poverty reduction, and humanitarian aid. But patronage politics and serious rights failures, especially in Papua, mean the record does not support a clean “welfare as the overriding purpose” reading.

**Positive evidence**
- [President Jokowi Sends Off Humanitarian Aid for Palestinians, Sudanese](https://setkab.go.id/en/president-jokowi-sends-off-humanitarian-aid-for-palestinians-sudanese/) - Sekretariat Kabinet Republik Indonesia, 2024-04-03. Jokowi explicitly described the shipment as a humanitarian mission to help civilians suffering in Gaza and Sudan; this is direct evidence of welfare-centered public action. IDs: `6B.1`
- [Does Indonesia’s National Health Insurance Scheme mobile phone application, Mobile JKN, support health financing?](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240100893) - World Health Organization, 2024-12-06. WHO says JKN was built to improve access to health services and financial protection, and that Mobile JKN simplified enrollment, helped informal contributors pay, and lowered administrative costs; this supports an inference that welfare protection was built into governing practice. IDs: `6B.1`
- [Indonesia](https://www.who.int/about/accountability/results/who-results-report-2024-2025/country-profile/2024/indonesia) - World Health Organization, 2024. WHO’s country profile says Indonesia reached 90 percent coverage, lowered out-of-pocket costs, and improved access to essential services regardless of gender, age, or disability; that is direct welfare-protection evidence. IDs: `6B.1`
- [Indonesia Growth and Jobs Report: Running Faster, for Longer](https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/indonesia/publication/indonesia-growth-and-jobs-report-running-faster-for-longer-structural-transformation-productivity-and-good-jobs) - World Bank, 2024. The Bank says growth delivered jobs and poverty reduction, with unemployment falling from 9 to 5 percent and poverty from 19 to 9 percent since 2000; that supports the inference that the state’s economic trajectory was broadly welfare-improving. IDs: `6B.1`
- [Macro Poverty Outlook for Indonesia: October 2024 Datasheet](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099026110152411280) - World Bank, 2024-10-02. The World Bank says Indonesia was growing at about 5 percent, poverty fell from 17.5 percent in 2023 to 15.8 percent in 2024, and external financing/currency pressures moderated; this supports the inference that welfare conditions improved despite constraints. IDs: `6B.1`

**Negative evidence**
- [Indonesia: Jokowi’s Term Ends with a Whimper on Rights](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/indonesia-jokowis-term-ends-whimper-rights) - Human Rights Watch, 2024-01-11. HRW says Jokowi’s final year produced no major initiative to address discrimination against marginalized groups, and that the new criminal code threatened speech and minority rights; this cuts against the claim that human welfare was the core governing purpose for all groups. IDs: `6B.1`
- [Indonesia: Racism, Discrimination Against Indigenous Papuans](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/18/indonesia-racism-discrimination-against-indigenous-papuans) - Human Rights Watch, 2024-09-18. HRW says Indonesian security forces committed arbitrary arrests, torture, extrajudicial killings, and mass displacement in Papua, and were seldom held accountable; that is strong evidence against a welfare-first governing orientation. IDs: `6B.1`
- [Analysis: A Decade of Jokowi, Indonesia’s Democracy Icon, Leaves Illiberal Legacy, Critics Say](https://theprint.in/world/analysis-a-decade-of-jokowi-indonesias-democracy-icon-leaves-illiberal-legacy-critics-say/2310394/) - Reuters via ThePrint, 2024-10-14. Reuters’ end-of-term analysis says Jokowi left patronage, dynastic politics, and weaker institutional integrity; this supports the view that welfare competed with family advantage and network preservation. IDs: `6B.1`

**Search gap**
Direct evidence about Jokowi’s private intent is limited. The strongest positive material is program/output evidence, not a confession of motive; the strongest negatives are patronage and human-rights patterns, not a direct statement that welfare was secondary. So the best-supported reading is “real welfare orientation, but not clean or exclusive.”
